discovery: Theoretical foundations of quantum computation and quantum simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Quantum optics / quantum information / atomic physics
motivation: Cirac and Zoller showed in 1995 how laser-cooled trapped ions could perform universal quantum logic. Their scheme turned the abstract idea of a quantum computer into a concrete physical architecture. It was soon realized experimentally and still underlies today's ion-trap processors. In 1998, with Jaksch and others, they proposed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices could realize the Bose-Hubbard model and its superfluid-Mott insulator transition. That proposal opened analogue quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter. They followed with schemes for entangling neutral atoms, Rydberg gates, quantum networks and repeaters, and synthetic gauge fields. Few theoretical contributions have moved so directly from proposal to decisive experiment, or seeded so many laboratories worldwide. Their work set the conceptual blueprint shared by quantum computing, quantum simulation and quantum communication with atoms, now a major branch of physics and technology.
